articles.title: 'Other generations just buried it' - Youths share their mental health concerns
articles.summary: The BBC's Catherine Burns spoke to some young mental health ambassadors who called for an increase in mental health support.
articles.body:
Accusations that those growing up today are a snowflake generation are wrong, the head of an independent review into mental health, ADHD and autism has said.

Prof Peter Fonagy told the BBC that there had been a real rise in mental distress among children and young people, with anxiety, depression, self-harm and eating disorders the most common.

His review was ordered nine months ago by Wes Streeting after the then-health secretary claimed in an interview that young people were over-diagnosed and "written off".

The BBC's Catherine Burns spoke to some young mental health ambassadors who echoed the report's findings and called for an increase in mental health support.

articles.title: Hydro project valve failure triggers flooding in Himachal Pradesh’s Kullu
articles.summary: Valve failure at NHPC Parbati-II hydro project caused water leakage, flooding Kullu’s Palchara/Rella area, damaging homes and fields; probe ordered.
articles.body: KULLU: A water leakage from the Parbati-II hydropower project flooded areas near Rella village in Himachal Pradesh’s Kullu district late Saturday, damaging houses and agriculture fields and forcing residents to flee.Water carrying muck and debris from a project dumping site surged downhill into Palchara village before draining into a nearby rivulet.Banjar sub-divisional magistrate (SDM) Pankaj Kumar, who visited the site on Sunday, told TOI the incident occurred near Adit 5, a horizontal access tunnel, at RD 14,000.“A technical malfunction in an air-pressure valve connected to the head-race tunnel allowed water to escape through the valve, causing the sudden discharge,” said the SDM. added that the air valve is designed to release air upwards, but due to the malfunction, water escaped through it, resulting in the sudden flow towards the area below.Preliminary assessment by the administration has put the damage to a house and other infrastructure at Rs 1 crore to Rs 1.5 crore, excluding losses to agriculture and horticulture.Villagers said the debris stored at the project’s muck dumping site aggravated the situation as it was carried downhill by the water flow.Rajender Chauhan, a Banjar resident, said the incident could have caused much greater damage had the flow taken a different direction.“It was sheer luck that the water turned towards the side it did. After damaging few houses, it flowed directly into a rivulet. If it had diverted towards the other side, Rella and the houses below the temple would have faced massive destruction,” Chauhan said.Environmental activist Guman Singh said the area has experienced land subsidence and sliding in the past.“All the villages of the panchayat, located below Adit 5, are situated on sloping terrain, where the soil is loose and friable. A dumping site is located behind Palchara and any failure of the debris or slope could cause extensive damage to the settlements located below,” said Singh. “During the monsoon in 2025, a landslide occurred here due to the debris dumped at the site, damaging two houses in the village. Ever since water was introduced into the tunnel last year, cracks have also appeared in the houses of many villages here including Raila village,” he said.The 800-MW Parbati Stage-II project is a run-of-the-river scheme on Parbati river, with an 83.7-metre-high concrete gravity dam at Pulga. The dam diverts the river water into a 31.56-km head race tunnel, which carries it underground to the powerhouse at Siund in Sainj valley.Probe orderedKullu administration has ordered an inquiry into the incident under the chairmanship of Sainj Tehsildar. Banjar SDM Pankaj Kumar said administration officials from departments concerned, along with teams from NHPC’s Parbati-II and Stage-III projects, would be part of the inquiry. “The committee will establish the reasons behind the malfunction and recommend measures, after proper study, to prevent such incidents in the future,” said SDM.2 yrs ago, Kangra faced damageThe flooding follows a similar incident in May 2024, when a penstock burst at the 25-MW Lambadug project in neighbouring Kangra district, inundating Multhan village with water and mud. The project water entered houses, shops and agricultural fields, destroyed standing crops and triggered a mud and debris slide that damaged property. articles.title: ICE officer shoots Venezuelan man delivering food in Austin, Texas, lawyer says
articles.summary: An ICE officer shot and seriously wounded a Venezuelan man Sunday afternoon as he was delivering food in Austin, Texas, his lawyer said.
articles.body:
An ICE officer shot and seriously wounded a Venezuelan man Sunday afternoon as he was delivering food in Austin, Texas, his lawyer said.

The man was taken to a local hospital and was "in serious but stable condition" after being shot in the torso, Austin-Travis County EMS Chief Robert Luckritz said at a news conference earlier.

The White House referred NBC News to the Department of Homeland Security for comment. A spokesperson for the DHS, the federal agency to which Immigration and Customs Enforcement belongs, said in a statement late Sunday that the man was stable and was in federal custody pending removal from the U.S.

Immigration attorney Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch identified him as Wilber Rafael Garcés Perez, 28.

He entered the country illegally under the Biden administration and had a final order of removal, the DHS spokesperson said, adding that Homeland Security Investigations, with help from the FBI, will lead an investigation into the shooting.

The shooting occurred around 1 p.m. in North Austin.

Texas Department of Public Safety spokesperson Sheridan Nolen said the agency received a request for assistance from ICE for a vehicle pursuit involving a blue Toyota Corolla.

A social media video verified by NBC News captures the sound of tires screeching followed by a person exiting a dark-colored SUV as a blue sedan is stopped next to it, both vehicles facing one another.

At least three gunshots are heard as the person approaches the sedan and runs up to it as it slowly lurches forward. The video shows the person standing next to the sedan's driver's side as it stops in front of an intersection. The sedan also appears to be damaged on the passenger side.

The shooting occurred before DPS troopers arrived at the scene, Nolen said.

"Once they arrived, DPS Troopers immediately began assisting partner law enforcement agencies in performing medical treatment on the driver of the Toyota Corolla," she said in a statement.

Lincoln-Goldfinch, who is representing the man, said lawyers for the hospital where he was treated indicated he had been released, though she wasn't sure at the time to whom.

The hospital, Dell Seton Medical Center at The University of Texas, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Lincoln-Goldfinch said she was with his wife at the hospital earlier, hoping to get information on his condition, but they were escorted from the premises.

"We are deeply concerned that his wife and family have not been permitted to see him and have not received a meaningful update regarding his current condition or whereabouts," Lincoln-Goldfinch said in a statement.

The man, who lives in Austin, is a DoorDash driver who was in the middle of a delivery when he was shot, Lincoln-Goldfinch said. In an email, a company spokesperson confirmed Garcés Perez was making a delivery at the time, adding that DoorDash is investigating and would not release more information "at this time."

Lincoln-Goldfinch told Telemundo Austin that her priority, and that of the man's family, is to find him and verify his condition.

"The main focus now is figuring out how and where he is, that he's OK, and then we'll be looking for justice," she said.

DHS has not provided any information about whether the ICE agent involved was wearing a body camera or if the man was the target of an operation or has any criminal background other than an immigration violation.

Austin Mayor Kirk Watson said the Austin Police Department was not involved in the incident.

Police Chief Lisa Davis said a "small foot pursuit" had occurred and that Austin police investigators were on the scene. Davis added that she was in contact with Homeland Security Investigations and other state law enforcement agencies.

"A person being shot on the streets of Austin by someone purporting to be law enforcement, particularly when it's ICE, is something that causes me to be unhappy and angry," Watson said at the news conference. "While I'm unhappy and I'm angry about it, I'm not surprised at all."

U.S. Rep. Greg Casar, D-Texas, demanded an independent investigation, the release of body camera footage and "accountability for any ICE officer who broke the law."

"Over and over, ICE has shot people and then lied about what happened. We can see the lies with our own eyes. We will demand truth, transparency and accountability," he said in a post on X .

In a letter addressed to DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin and Acting ICE Director David Venturella, Casar insisted on receiving a Congressional briefing by Sept. 28.

James Talarico, who is running as the Democratic candidate for one of Texas' U.S. Senate seats, said he is "closely following" reports of the shooting, and requested an investigation and all available footage.

U.S. Rep. Joaquin Castro, D-Texas, demanded "full accountability."

"Trump has allowed ICE to flood our streets and put our communities in harms way again and again," he said in a post on X .

In reaction to the shooting, the League of United Latin American Citizens — the largest Latino civil rights organization in the U.S. — called on Congress to establish an independent oversight of immigration enforcement.

Watson said he has asked for the city of Austin to be involved in any forthcoming investigations so that the police department can "be in a position to offer clear third-party eyes and expertise"

In a statement, the Travis County District Attorney's Office requested to be "co-equal partners in the investigation" and to receive cooperation from the federal government.

Protesters who gathered at the site of the shooting on Sunday afternoon and evening, next to an elevated stretch of Highway 183, shouted anti-ICE slogans in English and Spanish. Some carried signs that said, "Stop ICE murder," "Moms against ICE" and "Abolish ICE."

One woman, who said she has lived in Austin for 33 years, told NBC News earlier Sunday that she has never witnessed an incident like this and it "broke my heart."

The protest was punctuated with the sounds of drums, and someone could be heard saying, "They don't want you to be here" via loudspeaker.

Late Sunday night, the gathering roiled with tension, and Texas Department of Public Safety troopers responded by deploying tear gas and, in some instances, tackling protesters.

Protesters had dispersed and troopers appeared to have exited the area by 11 p.m. local time.

The shooting comes two months after an ICE officer fatally shot Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, a Mexican national, in Houston during an attempted traffic stop to conduct an immigration arrest. DHS has said Salgado Araujo was in the country illegally and attempted to run over agents, but it has not provided evidence of its claims.

articles.title: Redação Nota 10 encerra inscrições com mais de 300 textos enviados | G1
articles.standfirst: Banca examinadora vai avaliar os textos finalistas na quinta-feira (24); anúncio do vencedor e entrega dos prêmios acontecem no dia 28 de setembro.
articles.summary: Banca examinadora vai avaliar os textos finalistas na quinta-feira (24); anúncio do vencedor e entrega dos prêmios acontecem no dia 28 de setembro.
articles.body:
A 9ª edição do projeto Redação Nota 10, promovido pela TV Rio Sul, encerrou o período de inscrições com a marca de 313 textos recebidos.

Voltada para estudantes do ensino médio e da Educação de Jovens e Adultos (EJA) de escolas públicas e particulares das 24 cidades da área de cobertura da emissora, a iniciativa teve como tema deste ano: “Os desafios do uso da inteligência artificial na educação brasileira”.

Agora, o projeto entra na fase decisiva de avaliação. A banca examinadora, composta por professores convidados, se reúne na próxima quinta-feira (24), às 15h, na sede da TV Rio Sul, em Volta Redonda (RJ).

Durante o encontro, os finalistas serão avaliados com base em critérios como domínio da norma culta, clareza, originalidade e poder de argumentação.

O anúncio da redação campeã será realizado no dia 28 de setembro (segunda-feira), durante cerimônia oficial no auditório do Colégio Nossa Senhora do Rosário, também em Volta Redonda.

articles.title: Brasileira morta em Veneza: mãe pede ajuda para trazer corpo ao país | G1
articles.standfirst: Em vídeo publicado nas redes sociais, Gisele Elorriaga afirma que espera há mais de uma semana por uma solução e pede ajuda de autoridades do Brasil e da Itália.
articles.summary: Gisele Elorriaga pede auxílio às autoridades para o translado de Gabriela, brasileira morta em Veneza, após uma semana de espera por respostas na Itália.
articles.body:
A mãe da brasileira Gabriela Querino Elorriaga, de 26 anos, que morreu após um acidente entre embarcações na Lagoa de Veneza , na Itália, publicou um vídeo nas redes sociais nesta segunda-feira (21) pedindo ajuda para levar o corpo da filha ao Brasil.

No vídeo, Gisele Elorriaga diz que espera há mais de uma semana por respostas e que não sabe como conseguir o translado. Ela está em Veneza desde a noite de terça-feira (15).

"Eu preciso de ajuda do governo, não sei lá quem é, só para pedir a transferência dela, para levar embora. Não sei nem por onde começar", afirma.

Gisele diz que não está pedindo dinheiro. "Eu não quero dinheiro de ninguém. Eu só quero poder levar minha filha pra casa, gente. De poder fazer um velório, um enterro digno, é só isso."

Mãe de Gabriela Elorriaga pede ajuda para translado da filha ao Brasil — Foto: Reprodução/Redes Sociais

Em nota enviada ao g1 na semana passada, o Itamaraty informou que acompanha o caso por meio do Consulado-Geral do Brasil em Milão e que presta assistência consular à família, em contato com as autoridades italianas. O ministério disse que não fornece informações sobre casos individuais, por respeito à privacidade.

Segundo o Itamaraty, quando um brasileiro morre no exterior, embaixadas e consulados podem orientar os familiares, apoiar o contato com o governo local e emitir documentos, como o atestado consular de óbito, depois que as autoridades locais concluem os procedimentos obrigatórios.

Sobre o translado, o ministério afirmou que só realiza o de corpos de brasileiros mortos no exterior em situações excepcionais e devidamente motivadas, com base em decretos federais de 2017 e de 2025. O Itamaraty não informou se o caso de Gabriela está sendo avaliado dessa forma.

Natural de Ribeirão Preto (SP), Gabriela morreu depois que o barco em que estava com o marido, o pescador italiano Sean Michieli, de 25 anos, colidiu com um táxi aquático no Canal de Tessera, no dia 12 de setembro . O corpo dela foi encontrado três dias depois.

No vídeo, a mãe apela a autoridades do Brasil e da Itália, incluindo os presidentes dos dois países, governos, órgãos públicos e juízes, para que o translado seja feito com rapidez.

"É uma dor que eu não desejo pra ninguém. É a dor da perda, de não ter solução, de nada se resolver. É um desespero, uma agonia", diz.

O italiano Sean Michieli, de 25 anos, e a brasileira Gabriela Querino Elorriaga, de 26, em Veneza, na Itália. — Foto: Redes sociais

As autópsias nos corpos de Gabriela e de Sean estavam previstas para esta segunda-feira, segundo a advogada Mariarosa Cozza, que representa a família do italiano. De acordo com ela, só depois dos exames a situação do sepultamento seria definida.

Na semana passada, a imprensa italiana chegou a informar que a família de Gabriela pretendia sepultá-la ao lado de Sean, em Veneza. No vídeo, a mãe afirma que quer levar a filha para casa.

A Procuradoria de Veneza informou ao g1 que investiga o caso como homicídio culposo e naufrágio culposo e que o condutor do táxi aquático é investigado. O g1 tenta contato com a defesa do condutor, mas não obteve retorno até a última atualização desta reportagem.

articles.title: Mar avança rápido, destrói barcos e invade restaurante no Sul de SC | G1
articles.standfirst: Na Praia do Cardoso, em Laguna, o pescador André Eduardo Bento correu contra a correnteza para salvar embarcações. Ninguém ficou ferido durante o ocorrido.
articles.summary: Na Praia do Cardoso, em Laguna, o pescador André Eduardo Bento correu contra a correnteza para salvar embarcações. Ninguém ficou ferido durante o ocorrido.
articles.body:
O avanço rápido do mar assustou pescadores , destruiu barcos e invadiu um restaurante na manhã desta segunda-feira (21) no Sul de Santa Catarina. O fenômeno foi registrado em vídeos em ao menos duas cidades: Laguna e Jaguaruna ( assista acima ).

Em Laguna, a força da água invadiu a Praia do Cardoso antes mesmo das 6h . O pescador André Eduardo Bento relatou ao g1 que aguardava a melhoria do tempo para entrar no mar e iniciar o trabalho quando viu a onda avançando.

Para salvar o próprio barco e a embarcação de um amigo, ele correu contra a correnteza. Apesar do susto, ninguém ficou ferido.

"Quando o mar veio com tudo ali, a gente estava olhando para o mar. Nós corremos ali para pegar as nossas embarcações. Fiquei com água no peito e fui segurar a embarcação e a embarcação do outro rapaz porque senão o mar ia levar embora", contou.

Mar avança rápido, destrói barcos, invade restaurante e assusta pescadores no Sul de SC — Foto: André Eduardo Bento

Praia já foi atingida por tsunami meteorológico em 2023

Em 2023, a Praia do Cardoso já havia sido atingida por um tsunami meteorológico . Na época, André trabalhava como salva-vidas no local e também presenciou o fenômeno, que é considerado por especialistas como de difícil previsão .

A Secretaria da Proteção e Defesa Civil segue monitorando as condições meteorológicas nesta segunda-feira. Conforme o órgão, o estado está em alerta para rios, rajadas de vento, granizo e alagamentos , especialmente na região Sul.

A instabilidade ocorre por conta da aproximação e passagem de uma frente fria no estado que vem do Rio Grande do Sul e avança para as demais regiões ao longo do dia, ganhando força entre a tarde e à noite.

articles.title: China confirma visita de Xi aos EUA nesta semana | G1
articles.standfirst: Líder chinês terá reuniões com o presidente norte-americano Donald Trump em Washington. Eles tratarão sobre grandes questões relacionadas às relações bilaterais dos dois países e a paz e o desenvolvimento mundiais, segundo Pequim.
articles.summary: Líder chinês terá reuniões com o presidente norte-americano Donald Trump em Washington. Eles tratarão sobre grandes questões relacionadas às relações bilaterais dos dois países e a paz e o desenvolvimento mundiais, segundo Pequim.
articles.body:
Donald Trump e Xi Jinping durante encontro em Pequim em 14 de maio de 2026 — Foto: BRENDAN SMIALOWSKI/Pool via REUTERS

O presidente da China, Xi Jinping, fará uma visita oficial aos Estados Unidos entre quarta e sexta-feira desta semana e terá reuniões com o presidente Donald Trump , confirmou nesta segunda-feira (21) o Ministério das Relações Exteriores de Pequim.

"Por convite do presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald J. Trump, o presidente Xi Jinping fará uma visita de Estado aos Estados Unidos de 23 a 25 de setembro", afirma um comunicado.

Durante as reuniões, Trump e Xi tratarão sobre grandes questões relacionadas às relações bilaterais dos dois países e a paz e o desenvolvimento mundiais, afirmou nesta segunda o porta-voz do Ministério das Relações Exteriores chinês, Guo Jiakun.

A confirmação ocorre após Xi Jinping ter deixado antes do previsto a cúpula dos Brics na semana passada, o que levantou rumores sobre sua saúde e jogou dúvidas sobre se sua visita aos EUA de fato ocorreria.

Este será o segundo encontro de cúpula entre os líderes das duas maiores potências econômicas mundiais em 2026, depois da visita de Trump a Pequim em maio, e o terceiro encontro presencial desde o retorno de Trump à Casa Branca em janeiro de 2025.

Jiakun disse também que Pequim "trabalhará com os Estados Unidos para enriquecer o conteúdo da relação de estabilidade estratégica construtiva entre China e Estados Unidos, reforçar o diálogo e a cooperação e administrar de maneira adequada as diferenças"

Os dois países, que são tratados como as duas grandes potências competidoras pela supremacia mundial atualmente, têm diversas divergências nos temas de comércio e tarifas, inteligência artificial, as guerras no Irã e na Ucrânia e o status de Taiwan.

Sobre as tarifas, Xi e Trump anunciaram em outubro de 2025 uma frágil trégua após meses de guerra comercial, consolidada na cúpula de maio.

articles.title: Acidente na PE-499: Ramon Roriz morre em colisão em Terra Nova | G1
articles.standfirst: Ramon Roriz viajava para aproveitar a Festa de Setembro em Terra Nova. Vítimas do segundo automóvel foram socorridas, mas não há informações sobre o estado de saúde.
articles.summary: Acidente na PE-499 em Terra Nova causa a morte de Ramon Roriz. Colisão entre dois carros deixou feridos levados ao hospital; prefeito emitiu nota de pesar.
articles.body:
Ramom Roriz morre em acidente envolvendo dos veículos na PE-499 em Terra Nova. — Foto: Reprodução/ Redes Sociais

Um acidente entre dois carros deixou um morto na rodovia PE-499, em Terra Nova , no Sertão de Pernambuco, na madrugada de domingo (20). A vítima, identificada como Ramon Roriz, estava em um dos veículos, fraturou o pescoço e morreu no local.

Os ocupantes do segundo carro foram socorridos e levados para um hospital da região. O estado de saúde deles não foi divulgado.

Ramom Roriz era conhecido por fazer trilhas de moto na região. Ele morava em Salgueiro e era irmão do médico Rômulo Roriz, que foi vice-prefeito de Belém do São Francisco . No momento da batida, ele viajava de Salgueiro para Terra Nova para ir à Festa de Setembro.

O prefeito de Terra Nova, Dinha Mororó, publicou uma nota de pesar nas redes sociais. No texto, ele lamentou a perda do amigo e destacou o legado da vítima.

"É com profundo pesar e um sentimento de imensa tristeza que o prefeito Dr. Dinha Mororo lamenta o falecimento do seu grande e estimado amigo pessoal, Ramon Roriz, ocorrido na madrugada deste domingo (20). Filho de Zeze Roriz e da professora Inacia, Ramon deixa um legado de afeto, carinho e amizade verdadeira que permanecerá vivo na memória de todos que tiveram o privilegio de conviver com ele. Neste momento de dor inestimavel, o prefeito Dr. Dinha Mororó expressa suas mais sinceras condolências à familia e aos demais amigos, rogando a Deus para que, em sua infinita misericordia, traga conforto e força para superar essa perda".

articles.title: Incêndio em Patos: Mulher e crianças são socorridas de apartamento | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, as vítimas perceberam o início das chamas e conseguiram sair do imóvel. Mulher precisou de atendimento após inalar fumaça.
articles.summary: Vítimas de incêndio em Patos conseguiram deixar o imóvel após chamas atingirem quase todos os cômodos; mulher precisou de atendimento por inalar fumaça.
articles.body:
Incêndio destrói apartamento e mulher e crianças são socorridas em Patos, PB — Foto: Reprodução/Corpo de Bombeiros

Uma mulher e duas crianças foram socorridas após um incêndio atingir um apartamento por volta de 1h30 do domingo (20), em Patos, no Sertão da Paraíba. Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, as vítimas estavam no imóvel quando perceberam o início das chamas.

Ainda de acordo com a corporação, o incêndio atingiu praticamente todos os cômodos do apartamento. Apenas um dos quartos, usado como suíte e localizado na parte da frente do imóvel, não foi atingido diretamente pelas chamas.

A mulher, identificada como Valdenira Ferreira de Araújo, estava no apartamento com as duas crianças. Ela inalou fumaça e precisou de atendimento médico. As três vítimas foram retiradas do imóvel e encaminhadas pelo Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) para uma unidade de saúde.

O Corpo de Bombeiros informou que os trabalhos de combate às chamas, rescaldo e ventilação do apartamento duraram cerca de três horas. Ainda segundo a corporação, móveis, eletrodomésticos e outros objetos foram consumidos pelo fogo ou danificados pelo calor e pela fumaça.

Valdenira relatou aos bombeiros que as chamas teriam começado no segundo quarto do apartamento, mas não soube informar o que provocou o incêndio.

Uma perícia deve ser solicitada para identificar as circunstâncias e a possível causa do incêndio.

articles.title: Why Trump’s $24.3 billion Saudi F-35 deal is raising concerns in US, Israel
articles.summary: International News: The Trump administration’s approval of a potential $24.3 billion sale of F-35 stealth fighter jets to Saudi Arabia has put a long-pursued defence deal.
articles.body: The Trump administration’s approval of a potential $24.3 billion sale of F-35 stealth fighter jets to Saudi Arabia has put a long-pursued defence deal on a new track.The proposed package includes 48 F-35 aircraft and 49 engines, but the sale is not final yet and still faces congressional review. If approved, Saudi Arabia would become only the second country in the Middle East to operate the advanced fighter after Israel.The decision is significant because the F-35 is one of the most advanced fighter aircraft in the US arsenal, and its proposed transfer to Saudi Arabia would mark a major expansion of the kingdom’s air warfare capabilities.The deal has also renewed scrutiny over its potential impact on the Middle East’s military balance, Saudi Arabia’s growing ties with China and the protection of sensitive US defence technology.According to Reuters, Trump administration had already agreed to a separate $142 billion defence package with Saudi Arabia in 2025For Saudi Arabia, the deal would represent a major upgrade to its air force. The F-35 is a fifth-generation fighter designed around stealth, advanced sensors and networked warfare capabilities.Why the deal is controversialThe biggest question surrounding the proposed sale is how it could affect the military balance in the Middle East. Israel has operated the F-35 for years and has long maintained that preserving its qualitative military edge is essential to its security.The US administration has argued that the proposed sale would not undermine the regional military balance. The aircraft and systems supplied to Saudi Arabia could also differ from Israel's F-35 configuration, which includes Israeli-specific modifications and capabilities. CNN reported that Israeli concerns nevertheless remain over the potential consequences of the transfer.Another concern around the deal is Saudi growing relations with China. Saudi Arabia has expanded its economic, technological and military relationship with Beijing in recent years. US officials and intelligence agencies have raised questions about whether China's access to Saudi facilities or its broader relationship with Riyadh could create a risk to sensitive F-35 technology.The United Arab Emirates had previously been offered F-35s, but its proposed acquisition eventually stalled amid US concerns over its relationship with China and the protection of American technology.The Congressional review will also be a major hurdle for the F-35 deal. Even though the Trump administration has approved the potential sale, lawmakers can review the deal and raise objections. The debate could involve not only Israel's security and China-related technology concerns, but also Saudi Arabia's wider record and the strategic implications of expanding US military cooperation with Riyadh.

articles.title: Lindsay Clancy's ex-husband says he forgave her so he would not be 'eaten up inside forever'
articles.summary: Patrick Clancy gives his first interview since his wife's mistrial over the killing of their three young children.
articles.body:
Warning: This story contains distressing details and discussion of attempted suicide

Patrick Clancy, the ex-husband of a US mother accused of murdering their three children, has said he would have been "eaten up inside forever" had he not forgiven her for their deaths.

In an interview with CBS, he also said he did the best he could as his then-wife Lindsay Clancy struggled with mental illness in the months leading up to the day she strangled their children.

Lindsay has not disputed that she killed them but her lawyers argued she should not be held legally responsible because she was suffering from severe mental illness.

A judge declared a mistrial in the case earlier this month after the jury said it could not reach a unanimous verdict on whether she was guilty of murder.

The prosecution had alleged that on 24 January 2023, Clancy intentionally strangled all of her children - Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, eight months - in their Duxbury, Massachusetts, home.

Clancy, now 36, was then left paralysed after jumping from a second-floor window. She attended the trial in a wheelchair.

Patrick Clancy testified during the trial about his ex-wife's declining mental health after giving birth.

Clancy's team said she had postpartum psychosis, a rare condition in which postpartum women can experience mania, depression or a mixture of both.

"I didn't know how to manage a postpartum illness. I think mental illness has this ability to be tragically deceptive," he told CBS, the BBC's US news partner.

It was her mental health that led to Patrick Clancy deciding later to forgive her.

"I saw headlines that said, you know, 'Killer Mom', and 'Baby Murderer', 'Monster'. And none of them were accurate," he said in the interview.

"I believe that it was her mental illness that caused that. So I shared those words. And I think when it comes to forgiveness, I also felt that if I didn't get there, I would be eaten up inside forever."

Asked if he felt he had failed in some way in this period leading up to the killings, he said: "I think I did the best I could with what I had at the time. And I live with the outcome. I live with it every day."

Living with his grief in the weeks after the tragedy became a struggle and he admitted having suicidal thoughts.

"I didn't think I would live to see my 35th birthday. And I was completely fine with it," he said.

During the seven week trial, Patrick was singled out online for wild vitriol and cover-up accusations .

There were claims he was to blame for the murders in some way. Thrust into the limelight, tabloids snapped photos of him travelling and with his new wife Rachel Danis.

The 36-year-old said the speculation was "deeply harmful to the legacy of my children. It is a huge distraction from what really matters here, which is perinatal mental health".

It was also "painful to see" for him personally.

"And it makes it difficult to be in public and it's possible that some of those people after seeing lie after lie after lie, they start to believe it and that's what we're left with," he said.

The intense scrutiny prompted him to move from Duxbury to New York City in a bid to seek anonymity.

Now he is starting a family with Danis and looking forward to telling his future children about their siblings.

"I think every parent can agree, you have different relationships with your kids, but they're all your kids. And I can't wait to tell them about their brothers and sister."

The mistrial leaves the case unresolved . Prosecutors have not said whether they will seek a retrial.

The next court hearing is scheduled for 29 September at Plymouth Superior Court in Massachusetts.

If you are suffering distress or despair and need support, you could speak to a health professional, or an organisation that offers support. Details of help available in many countries can be found at Befrienders Worldwide .

A list of UK organisations that can help is available here .

articles.title: Is Germany’s leader Friedrich Merz doomed as far right wins again?
articles.summary: Before Sunday’s regional elections, speculation was rife about Merz’s survival. In the aftermath, he is now fighting for his political life.
articles.body: “It is a disaster.” Those were the words of a forlorn-looking German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Sunday evening as he addressed his party in the seconds after regional elections handed his center-right Christian Democrats (CDU) their second and third electoral drubbings in a month. The elections in the north-eastern region of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and the city of Berlin not only reopen the barely healed wounds from the Saxony-Anhalt election on September 6, but have plunged the party to new depths of unpopularity. Voters are abandoning the CDU –– the party of Angela Merkel and Konrad Adenauer –– in their droves, for the far-right, pro-Russia and anti-migration Alternative for Germany (AfD). The AfD has once again demonstrated it is a major political force in this country. On Sunday, Merz ruled out stepping down, saying Germany requires “courage, steadfastness and patience. I will demonstrate these qualities as Chairman of the CDU and, above all, as Chancellor of our country.” Before Sunday speculation was rife about Merz’s survival. In the aftermath, he is now fighting for his political life. In Mecklenberg-Vorpommern, the CDU’s prospects of making it into the parliament are hanging by a thread. Needing 5% to reach the threshold, they currently sit at 4.9% on projections. The party’s previous worst regional election performance in 75 years was 9% in Bremen in 1951. The AfD is projected to win the election with 38.3% of the vote, in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, although it fell far short of a majority. In Berlin it came in third, but saw a 7% increase in its vote share. The CDU was the incumbent party in the German capital but has lost its grip on power there to the far-left Die Linke party, which is projected to come out on top. The CDU fell into second place. Sunday’s results, coupled with the trouncing in Saxony-Anhalt earlier this month, heap misery on an already beleaguered Merz. A situation that, some believe, means only one outcome is possible –– a ‘chancellor-swap.” “This is the worst possible result for Merz and the CDU,” Jana Puglierin, head of the European Council on Foreign Relations’ Berlin office, told CNN as the results were announced. She said she saw no viable option for Merz to continue to lead the government, adding: “He has definitely lost control over his own party, and he has lost authority big time… and there is no way to reinstall it.” Following the AfD’s election victory in Saxony-Anhalt, the party’s co-leader, Alice Weidel, declared there would be national elections in Germany before the end of the year. She doubled down on Sunday, saying “the CDU cannot continue with Friedrich Merz, with a weak chancellor.” With two more elections going against the CDU, and Merz’s popularity plunging, that assessment seems less speculative. “It’s not like Merz can just throw in the towel, nor does he want to,” Sudha David-Wilp, vice-president and senior fellow at the German Marshall Fund, a think tank, told CNN. “He’s still hanging on, but he’s not out of the woods yet.” Any such upheaval would have reverberations around Europe. Germany, the EU’s most populous and economically powerful nation, has long stood as a rock of political stability and is a key backer of Ukraine as it fights Russia. Tanking poll numbers The Christian Democrats have long been the dominant political force in Germany. Of the 10 chancellors since World War II, the party has held the post six times – including a mammoth 16 years under the Angela Merkel. An opinion poll from September encapsulates Merz’s woes. Levels of dissatisfaction across the country are eye-wateringly bad. Only 13% of Germans are happy with the job he is doing, according to a poll for ARD public television released earlier this month. David-Wilp told CNN that AfD victories in the elections had been “baked” into the CDU’s political calculus, but the magnitudes of the outcomes were worse than expected. “There is a feeling in the CDU that something has to happen in order to change the dynamic, because the AfD is on the march and threatening the very existence of the CDU,” she said. Whilst the regions that make up the former East Germany are AfD strongholds, Merz’s problem lies in the party’s rise in popularity across the country. In two other state elections this year the AfD doubled its percentage share of the vote, while winning neither. Nationally, too, opinion polling suggests the AfD would be Germany’s biggest political party were a snap general election to be held now. Merz arrived in office in May last year promising to halve the AfD’s vote share –– so far the opposite has been true. Turmoil in Germany Such was the pressure on the chancellor last week that the other CDU state premiers felt it necessary to rally around him. They issued a joint statement Wednesday saying public support comes from “listening” and “political action” not “through personnel debates,” but failed to mention him by name. Replacing a chancellor mid-term is not uncommon, but a removal under these circumstances is. It would also make Merz the shortest-serving chancellor since reunification. His conservatives and their grand coalition partner, the Social Democratic Party (SPD), would have to agree on his successor, no easy feat. For David-Wilp, replacing Merz would “really leave a crisis of leadership when everybody is looking to Berlin for it.” Puglierin said that Merz’s ascension to power had been accompanied by hope across Europe that he would restore stability after the disastrous previous coalition led by Olaf Scholz, and would “keep the club together” at a time when the United States under President Donald Trump was ripping up the “Pax Americana” that had underpinned international relations since World War II. Those hopes could end in disappointment, Puglierin said, “because the country is looking inward… We are struggling with our political system that is no longer functioning the way it has done since the Federal Republic was founded in 1949.” Merz’s problems – some his own, others not Merz’s issues began before he even formally had the keys to the chancellery. It took him two attempts to be officially confirmed as chancellor, an unprecedented scenario. Then he reneged on an election promise not to increase Germany’s borrowing, by unlocking half a trillion dollars of spending for defense and infrastructure. Puglierin said personal characteristics –– poor communication skills, impulsiveness and a lack of emotional control –– “have put people off him.” In April, Merz made questionable remarks about Trump’s war in Iran. The chancellor said the US president was being “humiliated” by Iran in efforts to end the war. The comments drew the ire of the president, and upended the charm offensive by Berlin toward the White House. Before Merz’s comments, one official had remarked to CNN that they were pleased to have remained one of the few allies who had not been lashed by the sharp-tongue of the US president. Yet there is also little denying that factors outside of Merz’s control have combined to create roadblocks to progress. “The geopolitical backdrop of challenges that Germany is facing –– the war against Ukraine, inflation in Germany and energy costs –– all mean the economic model has been overturned in Germany,” said David-Wilp. “Merz was never a beloved figure, or the first choice to be chancellor,” she added, but outside factors and his “inability to communicate has created a crisis for Berlin.” No other viable candidate? Merz may still be saved by the lack of an obvious successor as chancellor and the dire situation his removal would leave the government in. Neither member of Germany’s two-party coalition government wants it to collapse, said Puglierin, given polling numbers are not in their favor. A new coalition would likely mean a return to a three-party government, a formula which failed spectacularly in recent memory under Olaf Scholz. A repeat of that “won’t solve Merz’s problem(s),” said Puglierin. The other challenge lies in finding a competent candidate who is ready to take the reins. The name on many people’s lips is that of the 51-year-old governor of North Rhine-Westphalia, Hendrik Wüst. “He is viewed as the heir apparent in the CDU. He is not a seasoned politician, but he may have to stand up earlier than anticipated,” said David-Wilp. Wüst, formerly a lawyer, has led North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany’s most populous state and an industrial powerhouse, since 2021. One of the few remaining regions where the CDU has a stable majority, it has its own state election in early 2027. Wüst “would be eager to be chancellor one day, but not under these circumstances,” said Puglierin, adding that the election in North Rhine-Westphalia is crucial for the CDU. “To change horses (in the election) on such short notice is a risky game,” Puglierin said, but added that she believes Wüst is the only candidate the SPD would agree to work with were Merz to be out of the picture. Wüst, though, has said he wants to focus on winning the state election, and that Merz has his full support.

articles.title: Iran’s military says US preparing to resume strikes
articles.summary: Tehran threatens retaliation as Trump weighs military action while Qatar pushes to revive talks.
articles.body:
Iran’s central military command says it has received information that the United States is preparing to resume strikes on the country.

The warning, issued on Sunday by the Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters, which oversees Iran’s armed forces, raises the prospect of a new round of fighting after months of reduced direct attacks.

Tehran said any renewed US assault would bring retaliation against American bases and interests in the Middle East and warned regional countries against helping Washington.

The military command said states that allowed their territory or facilities to support US attacks would be “considered complicit” and could face an Iranian response.

US President Donald Trump told Fox News on Sunday that he was in a “ deciding mode ” over Iran and said his options included further military action, economic pressure or a deal.

He also said he would be open to meeting Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York this week.

Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi left Tehran on Sunday evening for the UN General Assembly in New York, state media announced, adding that he is making a brief stopover in Qatar.

Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf told lawmakers on Sunday that Tehran should use military force to push back its opponents before turning to diplomacy to secure any gains.

Tehran has told Qatari and Pakistani mediators that conditions for renewed talks include an end to the war and US attacks, the release of frozen Iranian funds and the lifting of the US naval blockade on Iranian ports.

Ghalibaf said the Strait of Hormuz would remain closed until Washington met what Iran says are its commitments under an earlier agreement.

Al Jazeera correspondent Tohid Asadi, reporting from Tehran, said Iranian officials were sending a deliberate two-track message, signalling that they remained open to diplomacy while preparing for renewed fighting.

Qatar, a Gulf state mediating between the two sides, says its officials are travelling between capitals and exchanging proposals aimed at restarting negotiations.

Qatari Foreign Ministry spokesperson Majed al-Ansari said Doha had heard assurances from US officials that Washington wanted an agreement.

The confrontation is already disrupting the Strait of Hormuz, a narrow waterway linking the Gulf to the Arabian Sea and a key route for global energy shipments.

Shipping data showed 12 commodity vessels crossed the strait over the weekend, down from 35 the previous weekend. The war began in late February after joint US-Israeli strikes on Iran.

A 60-day memorandum reached in June reduced full-scale fighting but expired last month, with attacks around Hormuz increasing since then.

Mark Pfeifle, a Republican strategist and former White House national security official, told Al Jazeera that both countries were “locked in this frozen conflict” and trying to increase pressure before possible diplomacy around the UN gathering.

articles.title: Three South Korean soldiers injured in DMZ blast near border, military says
articles.summary: Three South Korean military officers were injured Monday in an unexplained explosion while conducting an operation in the western sector of the Demilitarized Zone separating the two Koreas, Seoul’s Joint Chiefs of Staff said.
articles.body: SEOUL, South Korea — Three South Korean military officers were injured Monday in an unexplained explosion while conducting an operation in the western sector of the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) separating the two Koreas, Seoul’s Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) said. Two of the officers were evacuated by helicopter. The third was expected to be transported by road before also being airlifted, the JCS said in a statement, without providing further details on their condition. South Korean media reported the blast might have been caused by a mine. The explosion took place south of the Military Demarcation Line within the DMZ, the JCS said. The heavily fortified border has separated the countries since the 1950-1953 Korean War ended with an armistice rather than a peace treaty. Mine explosions and other blasts are a recurring hazard in and around the DMZ, where legacy devices and suspected stray mines have periodically injured military personnel on both sides. North Korean forces resumed fortification work starting in March near the border, including mine-laying ​and fence ​construction, media reports said. Earlier this month, South Korean lawmaker Yu Yong-weon said minefields and other installations built by North Korea crossed the Military Demarcation Line by about 30 to 50 feet at six locations in the western area of the DMZ.

articles.title: Afghanistan says three killed in Pakistani air attacks
articles.summary: Three members of one family killed in air raid on house in Kunar province, Afghan Taliban deputy spokesperson says.
articles.body:
At least three people have been killed in northeastern Afghanistan in Pakistani air raids, Afghan officials said.

Kunar provincial spokesperson Farid Dehqan told Al Jazeera that the air attack hit the Nurgal district at about 4am local time on Monday (23:30 GMT Sunday), killing three people and injuring four.

⁠Pakistan’s information ministry ⁠said that 28 “terrorists” were killed in ⁠air strikes on three ⁠targets ⁠in Afghanistan.

Taliban deputy spokesperson Hamdullah Fitrat said at least one house in Kunar, a mountainous province in northeastern Afghanistan, was hit in the attacks, killing three members of the same family and injuring four others

“In the Barmal district of Paktika province, two locations were bombarded, destroying one shop and one unoccupied house, with no casualties reported,” he said.

The attacks threaten to reignite tensions between the neighbours after nearly three months of relative calm.

Relations between the former allies have been strained since February, when the two sides fought their worst clashes in years.

The dispute centres on violence in Pakistan, with Islamabad accusing Kabul of harbouring armed groups that stage cross-border attacks from Afghan territory.

Afghanistan’s Taliban government denies the charges and says the violence is Pakistan’s internal problem.

The air raids on Monday come days after a Pakistan Taliban faction said it carried out a bombing attack on a mosque at a police facility in Kohat, northwestern Pakistan. The blast and subsequent gun battle killed at least 21 people, mostly police officers, Pakistani officials said.

Pakistan’s Ministry of Information warned Saturday that the country could hit fighters inside Afghanistan in response to attacks in Pakistan. The ministry blamed the Kohat attack on fighters it said were based in Afghanistan.

articles.title: What to expect at the UN General Assembly, the biggest event in world diplomacy
articles.summary: This week’s General Assembly will bring hundreds of diplomats and world leaders to the UN’s New York headquarters.
articles.body: Fear not, world leaders — the UN’s notorious escalator has been fixed in time for diplomacy’s biggest event of the year. That’s what outgoing United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres told reporters at his last press conference ahead of this week’s General Assembly, which will bring hundreds of diplomats and world leaders to the UN’s New York headquarters. Last year, US President Donald Trump accused the UN of sabotage after the escalator he was riding malfunctioned while he made his way to the General Assembly Hall. “I can tell you that we took additional measures in order to make sure that whoever goes around does not interact negatively with the escalator,” Guterres said Wednesday. Aside from negative interactions with people-movers, the UN General Assembly has its work cut out for it, and this year’s theme is “Restoring trust, managing transformation: A United Nations that delivers for all.” The General Assembly also kicks off ahead of Guterres’ own exit from his role at year-end as concerns about emerging AI models hover over the proceedings. Here’s what to expect as the UNGA’s “General Debate” – where leaders and officials take turns speaking from the organization’s signature stone podium – begins Tuesday. Dealmaking and meetings The high density of diplomats and world leaders makes the UNGA a prime spot for meetings on the sidelines of the main event. Trump is scheduled to meet with Gulf leaders on Tuesday to discuss the next phase of the war with Iran, two US officials told CNN. There will also be a “high-level” briefing for Trump’s Board of Peace during week, a source familiar with the matter told CNN. It’s a notable juxtaposition considering Trump once suggested that the board, meant to oversee the reconstruction of Gaza, “might” eventually replace the UN. Meanwhile, France plans to convene a follow-up meeting this week on the two-state solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, diplomatic sources said. France and several other Western countries announced their recognition of the State of Palestine during the UNGA proceedings last year. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he will hold a meeting with Trump in New York, as he had last year. Such a meeting would come after US special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met separately with Zelensky in Kyiv and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow earlier this month. Trump has spoken only with Putin in the weeks since that visit. Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said he would meet with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, according to Russian state media. The General Assembly is also a place where deals are struck or formalized. Months after threatening to annex Greenland by force, Trump is expected to sign an agreement negotiated with Denmark and Greenland that would hand the US “permanent control” over Greenlandic security. It’s unclear how the deal would differ from current arrangements, which grant the US a large military presence on the island. Who’s speaking? The speeches delivered from the General Assembly podium often attract attention for the behavior of the audience as much as the speakers themselves. Last year, numerous delegates left the auditorium while Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu spoke. In 2018, laughing delegates interrupted Trump’s speech as he outlined his administration’s achievements. Daniel Forti, head of UN affairs at the International Crisis Group, told CNN that the speakers list will set the tenor for this year’s assembly. “While it seems like we have over 130 heads of state or government coming, it’s actually going to be a much more mixed picture in terms of the signals that world leaders are providing to the UN,” Forti said. One big question is whether Chinese leader Xi Jinping will make a surprise appearance in New York. Xi is due to appear in Washington for a state visit while the General Assembly is underway. “It’ll be a very difficult split screen for the organization if you have Trump and Xi meeting in Washington, and you don’t have both of the world’s biggest powers engaging in UN diplomacy during High-Level Week,” Forti said. Asked about Xi’s schedule, Guterres told reporters that while he “would like to have President Xi Jinping with us,” he met with him “twice last month” and is unconcerned about the Chinese leader’s commitment to “a world order based on multilateralism with the UN at its center.” Other headline speakers include Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who will speak first Tuesday, and Netanyahu, who will speak Thursday, according to a preliminary list. Venezuelan acting President Delcy Rodríguez will make her UN debut on Thursday while her former boss, Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro, sits in jail mere miles away in Brooklyn. Rodríguez is expected to meet with Trump ahead of her address. Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas is slotted for a Thursday speaking time before Netanyahu. However, the Trump administration has again refused Abbas a visa, so he will almost certainly address the chamber via video. Even as it denies visas to Palestinian officials, the administration will allow Iran’s “core delegation,” which will include President Masoud Pezeshkian, to come to New York. “Consistent with our host country obligations, the core delegation from the Iranian regime will be able to attend UN General Assembly High Level Week,” a State Department spokesperson said Thursday. “The delegation will be under travel restrictions and will face prohibitions on the purchase of luxury and other goods per our (sanctions) policy,” they said. “The delegation is smaller than last year.” Pezeshkian speaking in New York while his country is actively engaged in combat with the United States is virtually unprecedented. The closest international equivalent might be Egyptian President Anwar Sadat’s 1977 visit to Israel while the two countries were technically at war — but even that was part of a larger peace process. Pezeshkian will travel to New York on Tuesday, a representative from his office said Monday, according to Iranian state media. Goodbye, UN There will be a few notable goodbyes at the UN this year: France’s Emmanuel Macron is making his final appearance at the General Assembly, as is Guterres. The race to replace Guterres before the end of the year will be front of mind for many attendees, Forti said. The current secretary-general is the “last of a previous era of globalist leaders” and spent much of his 10-year tenure focused on development financing, climate change and girding the UN for the rise of artificial intelligence. The last point is especially important to the outgoing leader; Guterres spent more than half of his last press conference speaking about AI. “Artificial intelligence will certainly be a major topic in my discussions with world leaders next week — and the United Nations will continue to explore practical ideas and approaches in the immediate days ahead,” Guterres told reporters. After several weeks of apocalyptic warnings about the technology, AI is a top-billed issue for the UNGA this year. On Monday, tech industry figures, diplomats and the actor Joseph Gordon-Levitt are meeting for a conference on “Digital Cooperation.” The Security Council is slotted to meet about AI on Wednesday, and the US is hosting another event the same day. Guterres has been outspoken on AI since 2021, and his focus on the emerging tech may have come at the expense of his traditional role in promoting UN peacekeeping efforts, Forti said. “Guterres has certainly been very conservative and cautious on the UN’s role in peace and security,” he said. “He certainly has not made the most of the mandate and legitimacy that the UN carries to try and inject the organization into more peace-making efforts.” The secretary-general’s last speech is his opportunity to defend his tenure as the UN’s leader, Forti added. “It may fall on deaf ears,” the analyst said, “but in the long run, there may be more positive reflections on how he fought through a very difficult period.” An informal UN Security Council straw poll for Guterres’ successor was held Friday, with sources telling Reuters that Costa Rica’s former Vice President Rebeca Grynspan has a narrow lead. The US has yet to formally back a candidate. However, a State Department spokesperson said candidates must “publicly commit to the changes we require.” “Any new Secretary General must return the UN to its primary purpose of maintaining peace and security in the world, rather than the absurd, politicized, woke ideology that has undermined the institution’s effectiveness,” they said. Money, money, money The 2026 General Assembly finds the UN on firmer financial footing than last year, when it faced a severe budget crisis as the US threatened to cut the organization off entirely. The Trump administration appears to have reconsidered at least some of its UN skepticism. Ahead of the General Assembly, the US government sent the UN $827 million in dues — a fraction of the approximately $4 billion that the US owes the UN but a not-insignificant amount for a body that in January was facing “imminent financial collapse.” Yet the UN General Assembly has also increasingly served as a forum for its critics to question whether it matters at all. Last year, Trump asked the assembly point-blank: “What is the purpose of the United Nations?” “It has such tremendous, tremendous potential, but it’s not even coming close to living up to that potential, for the most part,” Trump said. “At least for now, all they seem to do is write a really strongly worded letter and then never follow that letter up. It’s empty words, and empty words don’t solve war.” Despite questions about the UN’s legitimacy and its increasing marginalization, Forti insists that the United Nations still matters. “At this moment in world affairs, where we have more wars than in previous decades … everyone still needs a place to come together, to deconflict, to hash out the rules of the road,” the analyst said. “And quite frankly, the UN is the only organization with the legitimacy, with the legal mandates, the ability to convene every state around the world to actually tackle those things.”

articles.title: Russia election results show Putin’s party winning: What we know
articles.summary: With more than 90 percent votes counted, Putin’s United Russia appears poised for a landslide win.
articles.body:
Early results emerging from Russia’s first parliamentary elections since the launch of the full-fledged war on Ukraine show President Vladimir Putin’s party dominating the vote — an outcome widely predicted.

The election, which began on Friday and ended on Sunday to elect members of the lower house of parliament, the State Duma, is projected to see Putin’s United Russia maintain its hold amid a tightly controlled election in which opposition to the president’s policies remains limited.

Despite the lack of alternatives to United Russia, the Kremlin had positioned the vote as a chance for residents to have their say since the invasion of Ukraine in 2022 and amid economic hardship.

Most antiwar candidates have been barred from the ballot. Those who did run from the liberal Yabloko party said they feared for their freedom after two senior party figures were handed long jail terms before the election due to comments made about the Russia-Ukraine war.

Still, Yabloko’s leader, Nikolai Rybakov, demonstrably spoiled his ballot paper, writing his party’s name and the slogan “For peace”.

The state news agency TASS reported on Monday that 90.43 percent of ballots had been counted, according to data from the Central Election Commission (CEC). As counting progressed, The Associated Press reported later in the day 95 percent of results had been tabulated.

The CEC found that, as of Sunday night, voter turnout stood just below 57 percent.

United Russia led with 57.86 percent of the vote, with 225 deputies apportioned from party lists. In single-seat races, another 225 lawmakers will be chosen, and Putin’s party is also projected to win most of them.

So far, no surprises or upsets have been recorded.

TASS also reported, citing the Ministry of Digital Development, Communications and Mass Media, that more than 3.6 million people voted online.

Those voting included residents of four Ukrainian regions that Moscow illegally annexed in 2022 – Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson and Zaporizhia – as well as those in Crimea, which was taken in 2014. The United Nations and most of the world do not recognise Crimea and other occupied Ukrainian regions as part of Russia.

Other parties, like the Communist Party of the Russian Federation (CPRF), the ultranationalist Liberal Democratic Party of Russia (LDPR), New People and A Just Russia, all of which largely vote the same way as United Russia in parliament, trailed behind in the early election results but were still on course to win seats in the State Duma.

The vote breakdown showed the CPRF at 13.84 percent, the LDPR at 8.9 percent, New People at 7.94 percent, and A Just Russia at 4.95 percent, according to TASS.

But while the early results paint a predictable outcome, the Berlin-based think tank NEST, cofounded by Kremlin critic Mikhail Khodorkovsky, said the vote could produce awkward moments for the Kremlin at a time of economic strain.

NEST said the votes received by the CPRF and New People might in many cases amount to a silent protest against Putin and United Russia — even if these parties do not actually challenge the president on most issues.

“The consequences of the war are increasingly being felt within the country, and accumulated anxiety and frustration may translate into votes for the systemic opposition parties that the Kremlin has allowed to remain on the ballot,” it said in a note.

What were previous outcomes and when are final results expected?

During the 2021 State Duma elections, United Russia kept an absolute majority in the 450-seat lower house, holding 326 seats.

The CPRF was the second-largest party, winning 57 seats. It has remained a major force in Russian politics since the collapse of the Soviet Union.

The CEC will announce preliminary results and turnout on Monday, but the final results are unlikely before Friday, by which time all ballots are likely to be counted and other procedures required by law are completed, TASS reported.

What has Ukraine said on the Russian election?

Ukraine had denounced the election, which involved voters from the annexed regions, with officials calling it illegal.

Moscow accused Ukraine of attempting to sabotage the election after a wave of Ukrainian drone attacks targeted Moscow and other regions on Sunday, which TASS called the biggest of its kind since the war began in February 2022.

The attacks killed three people in the Moscow region and two in the Russian-held part of Kherson, including an election official, according to the regional governor and the election commission.

Moreover, a facility at Moscow’s oil refinery, which has been targeted before, was also damaged.

On Monday morning, a man was killed and three others were wounded in a Ukrainian drone attack on Russia’s Bryansk region, according to acting Governor Yegor Kovalchuk.

articles.title: Presley Gerber, son of Cindy Crawford, dies at 27
articles.summary: Presley Gerber, the son of supermodel Cindy Crawford, died Sunday, a family representative said in a statement.
articles.body: Presley Gerber, the son of supermodel Cindy Crawford, died Sunday, a family representative said in a statement. He was 27. Gerber died at a “rehab facility,” according to online records of the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner. No cause of death or further detail was given. “The family is asking for privacy during this very difficult and painful time,” a statement on behalf of his family said. Supermodel Crawford married businessman Rande Gerber in 1998, and they have two children. Gerber and his younger sister, Kaia, both became professional models, featuring in campaigns for Dolce & Gabbana and Calvin Klein, among others. At 18, Gerber featured alongside his mother in a 2018 ad to re-create her iconic 1992 Super Bowl commercial for Pepsi. He and his sister have spoken about their mother giving them professional space. “She has never lived vicariously through us,” Kaia Gerber said in a family interview with “TODAY” last year. “You are so not a stage mom,” she added, of her mother. Gerber had posted online frequently about his struggles with depression and addiction. He instigated a program called “Mental Health Mondays” on his Instagram account, where he spoke openly about his struggles. He said in doing so he had hoped to “spark real conversations about the stuff most people hide.” In November, he wrote that he “had to step back and take care of my own mental health for a bit.” In an interview with Vogue magazine last month, his sister spoke about his struggles. “My parents for most of our lives were very, very private and didn’t share anything — and now we have this absolute teacher, my brother, who says, ‘I’m gonna be very human for everyone,’” she said. “There’s only so much you can hide from the world. And trying to put a lid on something just makes the person feel like you’re ashamed of them.” In July, for her son’s 27th birthday, Crawford posted two images online featuring Gerber as a child and as a young teenager, writing: “I’m so proud of the man you’ve become, but I’ll always see you as my little boy! Love you.” If you or someone you know is struggling or in emotional distress, call or text 988 or chat at 988lifeline.org 24/7 to reach the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline. For additional resources, visit SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources.

articles.title: Trump should press Xi on China’s persecution of believers at home and abroad
articles.summary: Pastor Ezra Jin's release from a Chinese prison spotlights the CCP's vast apparatus of religious persecution ahead of Xi Jinping's Washington visit.
articles.body: "A China without religious freedom is a China we cannot accept," Pastor Ezra Jin told a small group gathered on Capitol Hill shortly after he was freed from a Chinese prison. President Donald Trump had raised Jin’s case with Chinese President Xi Jinping at their May summit. Weeks later, Jin was free. But why was he in jail in the first place? He pastored the Zion Church in Beijing, an independent Christian house church outside the control of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP). PASTOR FREED FROM CHINESE PRISON AFTER TRUMP RAISED HIS CASE WITH XI JINPING Any and all religious groups in China must come under the control of the CCP or be subject to harassment, arrest, closure or worse. Forced organ harvesting of Falun Gong practitioners has been well documented. Falun Gong is a Chinese spiritual movement that the CCP particularly singles out for harsh treatment. Ten Chinese Catholic bishops — 10 — are currently in some form of detention in China for refusing to toe the CCP line. Cardinal Joseph Zen of Hong Kong was recently convicted of failing to properly register a charity fund. He is 94 years old and has been a respected leader in Hong Kong for decades, but not anymore in Xi’s China. Zen does not support the secret deal between the Chinese government and the Vatican over the appointment of Catholic bishops in China. THE CCP’S NEW ‘UNITY’ LAW TURNS CHINA’S REPRESSION INTO A GLOBAL THREAT The Panchen Lama, Gedhun Choekyi Nyima, the second-highest spiritual authority in Tibetan Buddhism, was abducted by the Chinese government 31 years ago. His current location is still unknown. Details differ, but the underlying pattern is the same. Religious leaders and communities not controlled by Beijing face intimidation, detention, disappearance or worse. BISHOP ROBERT BARRON: THE WAR ON CHRISTIANS IS REAL AND THE WORLD CAN NO LONGER STAY SILENT This system of religious control by the state is completely counter to the UN’s Universal Declaration of Human Rights and our own belief that the soul of every individual on the planet is entitled to be free to determine its own eternal destiny. A system that controls the most sacred right of the person is not a system we can support with our economic activity. Beijing’s oppression doesn’t stop at its own borders. The CCP is increasingly waging a campaign of harassment, disinformation and lawfare — called transnational repression — against religious and political dissidents in the United States. Falun Gong practitioners alone have suffered nearly 300 bomb and death threats. Not to mention the persecution of them still raging within China itself, where more than 5,000 confirmed deaths of Falun Gong practitioners have been recorded since the crackdown began in 1999. Just days ago, Anthropic reported disrupting China-based intelligence operations using its Claude AI platform to build surveillance dossiers on overseas dissidents and Tibetan Buddhist, Falun Gong, Christian and Uyghur communities, including the U.S. Beijing has a proven pattern of exploiting American institutions and technology to harass and oppress dissidents who had thought they had reached the safety of America. BRONX MAN CONVICTED OF RUNNING SECRET CHINESE POLICE STATION IN MANHATTAN USED TO MONITOR DISSIDENTS Xi is scheduled to be in Washington starting on Sept. 24. Trump should make this system of coercion and control a point of discussion. Countries that won’t even allow their own people to worship freely are not reliable trading partners and certainly not countries we want to prop up with our dollars. They may provide us with cheap goods, but our souls, and those of others, are not for sale at any price. Details differ, but the underlying pattern is the same. Religious leaders and communities not controlled by Beijing face intimidation, detention, disappearance or worse. Communism officially denies the existence of God and establishes government as the highest authority in the universe. Therefore, everything is under its control unless it specifically permits freedom. A person’s rights come from the government, not from God or anywhere else. TRUMP SAYS CHINESE PRESIDENT XI JINPING WILL VISIT US ON SEPT 24 Communists, authoritarians and totalitarians figured out long ago that "religious people" must be controlled because they choose to answer to a higher authority — an allegiance that fortifies their willingness to confront and defy government when it is in the wrong, even at the cost of their property, freedom or lives. Sounds like the kind of people we want to advocate for! Think of the Jewish refuseniks and evangelicals of the late Soviet era who confronted that evil regime, or the Christians in Burma who stand against the ruling military junta today. But freedom comes at a cost. That’s why it’s so precious. The cost to us is not our freedom, as it is for the Chinese Christians, Buddhists, Falun Gong practitioners or Uyghur Muslims. It is our willingness to stand up to China. Trump is the first president since John F. Kennedy to confront China, and he should be applauded for it — and encouraged to go further. He raised tariffs on an evil Communist regime that seeks world dominance. He has confronted and weakened China’s allies in Iran, Venezuela, Cuba and elsewhere. He should continue to exert that leverage on behalf of people whose only offense is refusing to place their faith on the altar of the Chinese Communist Party. Now is the time to confront the CCP’s extensive apparatus of religious oppression — just as Reagan confronted the Soviet system — and make clear that the Chinese people should not have to choose between their faith and freedom.
